values.rule: A source says the tool does it, as the dimension defines yes.
A source says the tool does part of it, as the dimension defines partial. Where a reading was ambiguous, the one harder on the tool was taken and the note says so.
A source says the tool does not do it, or defines the tool's scope so that it structurally cannot (the note says so then). A page that is silent is not a source for no: that cell is unknown.
No public source we could read says it. It does not mean no. It has no source.
Assessed tool only: designed or built and not on main. Never counted as yes.
The cell is text, not a verdict: the dimension is informational.

dimensions.name: Languages
dimensions.definition: The languages the tool analyses or edits, as its own documentation lists them. Cell text: the list or the count.

dimensions.name: Front end
dimensions.definition: How source is read: compiler front end (type-checked, from the language's own compiler or type checker), build-intercepting extractor (runs the real build), tree-sitter, own parser, bytecode, or an index produced by a compiler. Cell text: the kind.

dimensions.name: Typed model
dimensions.definition: Every expression of the model the analysis runs on has a resolved type.

decision.yes: types resolved for every expression in the supported languages.
decision.partial: types for some languages or some constructs.

dimensions.name: One IR across languages
dimensions.definition: One intermediate representation or fact schema serves all supported languages, so one analysis runs on all.

decision.partial: one for a family of languages, or a shared core with per-language extensions.

dimensions.name: Documented, versioned IR schema
dimensions.definition: The IR or fact schema is a public document with a version identifier.

decision.partial: public schema (or library API reference) without a version contract.

dimensions.name: Policy on a construct it cannot model
dimensions.definition: What happens at a construct outside the model.

decision.yes: refuse or mark unknown, with a reason and a position, kept in the output.
decision.partial: warn or diagnose but continue with an approximation.
decision.no: approximate silently, or documentation does not say and the design is heuristic.

dimensions.name: Coverage measured and reported
dimensions.definition: The tool reports, per run, how much of the code it read or analysed (files, functions, lines, extraction success).

decision.yes: a per-run coverage figure or report.
decision.partial: only error or warning counts, or partial.

dimensions.name: Absent versus unseen
dimensions.definition: A query or finding distinguishes 'not found' from 'could not see' (three-valued or possible/definite answers).

decision.partial: partial (for example only an incompleteness warning).

dimensions.name: Query style
dimensions.definition: The form of a user-written query: Datalog-like, object-oriented query language, pattern by example, graph traversal DSL, API (library code), rule configuration only, none. Cell text: the form.

dimensions.name: User-authored rules
dimensions.definition: Users can write their own checks or queries.

decision.partial: possible only through a library API or by forking.

dimensions.name: Recursion in user queries
dimensions.definition: The query language supports recursion (transitive closure) written by the user.

decision.partial: through built-in closure operators only.

dimensions.name: Control-flow paths in queries
dimensions.definition: A query can ask about paths in the control-flow graph: 'on every path', 'before/after', dominance.

decision.partial: partial (for example path-insensitive 'ellipsis' matching or built-in checks only).

dimensions.name: Interprocedural analysis
dimensions.definition: Analysis follows calls across function boundaries through a call graph.

decision.partial: limited (for example one file, or one level).

dimensions.name: Dynamic-dispatch resolution
dimensions.definition: Calls through interfaces or function values are resolved by a documented algorithm (CHA, RTA, points-to, or equivalent).

decision.partial: heuristic or limited.

dimensions.name: Effects and syscalls
dimensions.definition: Reports what a function may do outside its own memory (file system, network, process, environment, syscalls) as a result of the analysis.

decision.yes: built-in effect or capability report per function.
decision.partial: only through user-written queries or source/sink models.

dimensions.name: Taint tracking
dimensions.definition: Tracks data from sources to sinks.

decision.partial: intraprocedural or file-local, or limited to some languages or a paid tier.

dimensions.name: Scope of one run
dimensions.definition: Per file, per compilation unit or project, or whole program including libraries. Cell text: the scope.

dimensions.name: Third-party dependencies
dimensions.definition: Dependencies are analysed in the same graph as the project.

decision.yes: dependency source or bytecode read and analysed with the project.
decision.partial: summaries or models of libraries, or vulnerability matching on versions only.

dimensions.name: Diff of two revisions with stable identities
dimensions.definition: Compares analysis results of two revisions of a program and reports what changed, naming items by identities that survive moved lines.

decision.partial: partial (for example finding fingerprints, baseline comparison, or a diff-aware scan without a fact diff).

dimensions.name: Code edits
dimensions.definition: Applies source changes (autofix, codemod, refactoring) driven by a query or pattern.

decision.partial: only suggested fixes, or limited to some rules.

dimensions.name: Edit verified by re-reading
dimensions.definition: An edit is checked before it is written, by re-reading or rebuilding the result and comparing it with the expected result.

decision.partial: syntax re-parse or compile check only, or by running tests.

dimensions.name: Translation between languages
dimensions.definition: Reads one language and writes another from the same model.

dimensions.name: Behaviour check of a translation
dimensions.definition: A translation or rewrite is checked by running original and output on the same inputs.

dimensions.name: Conformance kit for third-party adapters
dimensions.definition: A published test kit lets an outside author check a front end or adapter against a feature list.

decision.partial: a testing guide or harness without a feature vocabulary.

dimensions.name: Documented determinism
dimensions.definition: Documentation states that the same input gives byte-identical output (or tests it).

decision.partial: stated for part of the output.

dimensions.name: Licence
dimensions.definition: The licence of the engine and, where different, of the rules or query libraries. Cell text: the licence.

dimensions.name: Self-hosted and offline
dimensions.definition: Runs on the user's own machine or infrastructure without sending code to a vendor service.

decision.partial: yes for the engine but a paid tier or cloud is needed for some features.

dimensions.name: CI integration
dimensions.definition: Documented way to run in CI (official action, plugin or CI guide).

decision.partial: command line only.

dimensions.name: Output formats
dimensions.definition: Machine-readable result formats the tool documents (SARIF, JSON, XML, CSV, other). Cell text: the list.

dimensions.name: Ships a maintained rule catalogue
dimensions.definition: The project or vendor ships and maintains ready-made rules or queries.

decision.partial: examples only.

stands_out.title: Answers that say what they could not see (S3)
stands_out.text: codespec is the only column with `yes`: a result carries `definite` or `possible` and the unknown sites that made it possible [^codespec-S3]. CodeQL is `no` (global flow drops paths "and no warning is given") [^codeql-S3], SCIP and ast-grep are `no` [^scip-S3] [^ast-grep-S3]; Semgrep, Infer, SpotBugs, Capslock, OpenRewrite and Coccinelle reach `partial` through incompleteness warnings only [^semgrep-ce-S3] [^infer-S3] [^spotbugs-S3] [^capslock-S3] [^openrewrite-S3] [^coccinelle-S3]; the rest are `unknown`.

stands_out.title: A conformance kit for third-party adapters (E1)
stands_out.text: codespec ships a kit of one case per feature id and a command that gives per-feature verdicts [^codespec-E1]. The nearest others are `partial`: test harnesses with no feature vocabulary or verdicts [^semgrep-ce-E1] [^scip-E1] [^go-analysis-E1]. All others are `unknown`.

stands_out.title: Reading one language and writing another from the same model, checked by running both (C4, C5)
stands_out.text: codespec is the only column with `yes` on both [^codespec-C4] [^codespec-C5]. Every other column is `no` or `unknown` on translation [^openrewrite-C4] [^ast-grep-C4] [^coccinelle-C4].

stands_out.title: A written edit is read again and must equal the expected model before it is printed or written (C3)
stands_out.text: codespec is `yes` [^codespec-C3]. The only other `yes` is Snyk Code, whose engine re-checks each machine-proposed fix inside the vendor's cloud service [^snyk-code-C3]; the open codemod tools stop at a test-time comparison or a syntax check [^openrewrite-C3] [^ast-grep-C3].

stands_out.title: Documented determinism (E2)
stands_out.text: codespec states and tests that the same input gives the same bytes [^codespec-E2]. Others are at most `partial` (a stated part: [^clang-sa-E2] [^go-analysis-E2] [^capslock-E2]) and Infer documents non-determinism [^infer-E2]. The rest are `unknown`.

stands_out.title: Refusal with a reason as the policy for unmodelled constructs (S1)
stands_out.text: `yes` for codespec [^codespec-S1] and for one other, Capslock, which marks unanalysable paths `UNANALYZED` [^capslock-S1]. CodeQL, Semgrep, Joern, Infer and others continue with a diagnostic or an approximation (`partial`) [^codeql-S1] [^semgrep-ce-S1] [^joern-S1] [^infer-S1].

stands_out.title: Effects and syscalls per function, with call sites (A3)
stands_out.text: `yes` for codespec and Capslock only [^codespec-A3] [^capslock-A3]. Both are limited to one ecosystem: codespec's syscall barrier exists for Go on linux/amd64 only [^codespec-A3].

stands_out.title: The combination
stands_out.text: One typed model for all readers (L3), one IR for all languages (R1), a documented versioned schema (R2), three-valued answers (S3), user recursion (Q3) and control-flow path queries (Q4) are all `yes` for codespec and for no other column. Joern is next: `yes` on R1, R2 and Q4, `partial` on L3 and Q3, `unknown` on S3 [^joern-R1] [^joern-R2] [^joern-Q4] [^joern-L3] [^joern-Q3] [^joern-S3]. Capslock is `yes` on L3 and S1 and `no` on R1 [^capslock-L3] [^capslock-S1] [^capslock-R1]. The query language is Datalog in the CodeQL and Soufflé tradition [^codespec-Q1]; the difference is the typed model and the definite or possible answer.

behind.title: Language breadth and depth (L1)
behind.text: codespec reads eight languages, each a subset [^codespec-L1]; SonarQube lists 47 [^sonarqube-L1], CodeQL 12 [^codeql-L1]. By the project's own support matrix the Go reader verifies 115 of 121 applicable features and the Rust reader 113, while the Elixir, Gleam and Odin readers verify 30, 25 and 28 (counts of `verified` cells in `website/data/support-matrix.json` at the assessed revision). On real code the Go reader reads a fraction of the standard library's functions: 10.5 % of `syscall`, 28.3 % of `runtime`, 46.8 % of `os` [@website/docs/guides/map-a-repository-to-syscalls.md:66-77].

behind.title: Dependencies (A6)
behind.text: `partial`: only Go has a dependency reading path [^codespec-A6]. Capslock, Doop and the Go analysis framework are `yes` [^capslock-A6] [^doop-A6] [^go-analysis-A6].

behind.title: Precision of the effect analysis
behind.text: Dispatch over the whole standard library is wide: with `cha` most functions that do IO share one large component, and the measured entry point of one library leaves 155 reachable functions `unknown` (66 interface calls, 59 function values, 27 runtime functions) [@docs/static-analysis.md:218-226]. The effect summaries are claims not yet checked against a run [@docs/static-analysis.md:235-241].

behind.title: Points-to and pattern authoring
behind.text: Points-to analysis beyond dispatch is out of scope [@docs/query-language.md:330]; Doop is built on it [^doop-A2]. Writing a query by example in source syntax, as Semgrep and ast-grep do, is planned for cq [@docs/query-language.md:325], not shipped [^semgrep-ce-Q1] [^ast-grep-Q1].

caveats: The dimension list is ours. It follows what codespec does, so it is kind to codespec on change, translation and conformance, which most tools do not try to do, and it leaves out dimensions where other tools lead: IDE integration, hosted dashboards, ticket integration, size of the rule community, breadth of languages with deep semantic analysis.
The cells about codespec were written by the group that maintains codespec. Check them against the cited lines.
Several `no` cells for analysis-only tools on C2 to C5 rest on scope pages, not on a statement that the feature is absent. The note of the cell says which.

Public documentation may lag the code, in both directions. codespec's own pages disagree in two places we found: `docs/conformance.md:3` still says "proposed, not implemented" while the status page, the CLI reference and the kit show it shipped; `docs/static-analysis.md` and `docs/query-language.md:155` say only the Go reader lists calls, while `CHANGELOG.md` records call lists for the Rust and Groovy readers. The cells follow the shipped behaviour in the changelog and the CLI reference.
API-only tools (go/analysis, SpotBugs, Error Prone, Clang) have no query language; their Q3 is `partial` (recursion in host-language code). Single-language tools are `no` on R1.
OpenRewrite is assessed as the open-source engine, Semgrep as two columns by tier, SonarQube as the self-managed product with the edition named in a cell where it differs.
